clue.text: Focus one's attention on money in box

indicators.note: the words 'on money' are placed in the box, so they sit inside its letters

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box
taken as written
a cent is a small coin, so money

explanation.surface: Advice to keep your mind on the cash in the box.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a phrasal verb with 'on'; here 'on' is a piece of the wordplay, and the rest is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To concentrate is to fix the mind closely on one thing.

clue.text: What we have is time we hear

indicators.note: says the word for time is to be heard spoken, and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: hours are units of time

explanation.surface: Someone muses that what we own is merely time.
explanation.walkthrough: With the H silent, as in 'hour', HOURS is said the same as OURS.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for belongings shared by us.

clue.text: Get rid of players on strike

parts.note: the cast are the actors in a play
workers who have walked out are 'out'

explanation.surface: A theatre manager wants to fire the actors who have walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast out is to expel or banish.

clue.text: One's upset by what smells

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, with the S counted

explanation.surface: Someone is offended by a bad odour.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is the organ of smell.

clue.text: Stretches between bends

explanation.definitionFit: Stretches is a verb for extends; a river's straight sections between bends have the same name.

clue.text: They are driven from the river

explanation.definitionFit: Golfers drive the ball off small pegs; the Tees is a river in northern England.

clue.text: Intuition supported by Richard III, possibly

parts.note: a hunch is an intuitive feeling
backed means supported

explanation.surface: A gut feeling confirmed by a historical king.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Richard III is portrayed with a crooked back; 'possibly' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard III is traditionally depicted with a humped spine, an example of the condition.

clue.text: Evergreen creepers

parts.note: reads as climbing plants that keep their leaves, but means reptiles that creep through the green lawn

explanation.definitionFit: Grass is green and these reptiles slither through it.

clue.text: Early impression the reader may have to correct

definitions.text: Early impression the reader may have to correct

parts.words: Early impression the reader may have to correct
parts.note: sounds like a first opinion one revises, but means a trial print checked by a proofreader

explanation.definitionFit: A printer's trial sheet pulled before final printing, for a reader to mark errors.

clue.text: Labour leader may give the password

definitions.text: Labour leader may give the password

parts.words: Labour leader may give the password
parts.note: suggests the head of the Labour party, but means a union official at a workplace who passes the word to the members

explanation.definitionFit: A union representative elected by workers in a factory, leading them at plant level.

clue.text: Seen in a list perhaps, but it's not necessary

indicators.note: perhaps tells us the letters of these words may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Something spotted in a list is judged not to be needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals an anagram of SEEN IN A LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Inessential means dispensable, not required.

clue.text: It could kill, though it's not down as a poison

parts.note: the opposite of down is up
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that something lethal is not as harmless as it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: The upas is a Javan tree whose sap was used as arrow poison; 'It could kill, though it's' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: The milky sap of this tropical tree is toxic, used for poisoned arrows.

clue.text: A command to avoid

explanation.definitionFit: A clipped drill order for 'attention'; also a verb meaning keep away from.

clue.text: Being hardened, a summons is nothing to us

parts.note: a call is a summons
O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thick-skinned shrugs that an official summons means nothing to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Callous describes someone emotionally hardened, unfeeling.

clue.text: In this way Sue mixed pickle

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of the name are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions on how Sue prepared her pickles.
explanation.definitionFit: To souse is to steep food in brine or vinegar.

clue.text: He lived with his wife and mother

definitions.text: He lived with his wife and mother

parts.words: He lived with his wife and mother
parts.note: sounds like a man sharing a home with his in-law, but his wife was also his mother

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this king of Thebes unknowingly married Jocasta, his own mother.

clue.text: Black magic?

parts.note: reads as sorcery in general, but points to a folk magic of West African and Caribbean origin

explanation.definitionFit: A form of sorcery practised in the Caribbean, rooted in West African tradition.

clue.text: Monuments to doctors?

parts.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree, so MBS for doctors

explanation.surface: A memorial erected to honour physicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand burial vaults are memorials to the dead.

clue.text: Barks from trees?

explanation.definitionFit: Hounds give deep howls; laurels are also named this.

clue.text: Number not in style, what an eyesore

indicators.note: the number is not in the word, so it is removed

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone dressed unfashionably is an ugly sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing L from STYLE leaves the answer; 'eyesore' is literal, a sore on the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful swelling on the eyelid is literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Numberless Visa account fora patriarch

indicators.note: the card name loses a number, the Roman numeral V for five

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A credit card account opened for an elder of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'fora', an OCR join of 'for a'. V is five in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the son of Abraham and father of Jacob is one of the Hebrew patriarchs.

clue.text: Concentrated on treating tennis elbow initially

indicators.note: treating suggests processing the word, so its letters are reworked
initially takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A physio focuses on treating tennis elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treating' turns TENNIS into INTENS, then 'initially' adds E from elbow.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means strong, highly focused.

clue.text: New act involves nude entertainment

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the other word
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: bare means nude

explanation.surface: A new stage act includes naked performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal on 'act', and 'involves' signals the container: the rearranged letters wrap the synonym for nude.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub show of songs and sketches.

clue.text: Red vehicle goes to one of the pits

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a mine is a pit, as in a coal pit

explanation.surface: A red car heads to a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a vivid crimson shade.

clue.text: Would it take another like him to be of one mind?

definitions.text: Would it take another like him to be of one mind?

parts.words: Would it take another like him to be of one mind?
parts.note: sounds like agreement, but two people each with half a brain would make one whole

explanation.definitionFit: A foolish person, one with half the usual wits.

clue.text: Land in the river

parts.note: describes a small island in a stream, a word used for those on the Thames

explanation.definitionFit: A small river islet, a word used especially on the Thames.

clue.text: Honest expression of agreement

explanation.definitionFit: Honest means sincere; saying 'very so' concedes a point.

clue.text: Hit a wild man from the East

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run unruly and land in a new order

explanation.surface: An eastern man lashes out wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Thailand in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Professional on a sailing vessel

parts.note: pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: An expert sailor aboard a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malay outrigger sailing boat.

clue.text: Leave with uncle

parts.note: sounds like a family arrangement, but 'uncle' is old slang for the moneylender who holds goods against a loan

explanation.definitionFit: To deposit an item with a moneylender as security for a loan.

clue.text: Pain!

parts.note: reads as a cry of hurt, but it is the French word for a loaf

explanation.definitionFit: In French 'pain' means the baked loaf, so a long baguette.

clue.text: Monk in glasses?

explanation.definitionFit: A member of the order of St Benedict; also a herbal liqueur served in small glasses.
